ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Companies Act 1993; Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009; Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism (Definitions) Regulations 2009; Income Tax Act 2007; Financial Markets Authority Act 2011. New Zealand does not maintain a public UBO register; beneficial ownership information is collected through AML/CFT customer due diligence and is made available only to competent authorities such as the Financial Intelligence Unit, Inland Revenue Department, New Zealand Police, Department of Internal Affairs and Financial Markets Authority.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: New Zealand is an Apostille Convention State. Authenticate through notarization by a New Zealand notary public followed by an Apostille Certificate issued by the New Zealand Department of Internal Affairs. Consular legalization is never chained to apostille. For non-Apostille receiving states, use the separate parallel path of notarization, authentication by the New Zealand Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade, and legalization by the destination-state consulate.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory protocols require screening of all directors, shareholders, beneficial owners, signatories and counterparties against the New Zealand Department of Internal Affairs AML/CFT Watchlist, the United States Office of Foreign Assets Control SDN List, the United Nations Consolidated Security Council List, and applicable domestic sanctions under the Russia Sanctions Act 2022. PEP screening must cover both domestic and foreign politically exposed persons, their immediate family members and close associates. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for PEP status, non-resident entities, complex or opaque ownership structures, and substantial cross-border wire flows. Adverse media checks and sanctions re-screening must be completed within 24 hours before name clearance and at least quarterly thereafter. Any positive hit must be escalated to the AML/CFT compliance officer, and where required reported to the New Zealand Financial Intelligence Unit under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Register Name Availability and Reservation Portal, administered by the New Zealand Companies Office of the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Statutory doctrine requires company names to be registered in English or te reo Maori transliterated into Latin script. Non-Latin scripts must be phonetically transliterated into the English alphabet for registration. The four-tier naming test requires a legal-form element such as Limited, a distinctive unique element, an unrestricted common element, and a restricted or sensitive element requiring ministerial or regulator consent. The Companies Office will register the English transliteration only, while non-Latin trade names may be used in commerce if the registered English name is the legal name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: An applicant whose proposed name is rejected may file a written objection with the Registrar of Companies within 20 working days of the decision, stating the statutory and factual grounds for distinguishing the proposed name from any conflicting registered name. The Registrar must reconsider and issue a signed determination. A further internal review by the Companies Office is available. If the Registrar maintains the refusal, the applicant may seek judicial review in the High Court of New Zealand under the Judicature Amendment Act 1972. The applicant may also reserve a different name immediately. Name reservations are not automatically extended; a fresh application and fee are required before expiry.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Under the Companies Act 1993, the registered office must be a physical street address in New Zealand and cannot be a P.O. Box. A virtual office with a dedicated physical New Zealand street address, mail forwarding, and registered-agent service is technically permissible for incorporation. However, New Zealand banks under AML/CFT customer due diligence ordinarily require a verifiable operating location or a substantive management relationship and may reject a pure commercial-mailbox profile for an ISIC 4791 B2B MRO e-commerce business. Inland Revenue may also scrutinize alleged tax residency and GST registration where there is no local operational substance. For this low-risk industry, a virtual office is acceptable if supported by a written office-service agreement, local directorship, and credible records evidencing management and control in New Zealand.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: current registered-office service agreement, physical street address, director appointment records, board minute book, share register, constitution, financial records, bank account mandate, and annual return filings. New Zealand does not conduct routine municipal unannounced inspections for corporate registration, but Inland Revenue may arrange a site visit under the Tax Administration Act 1994 when triggered by GST registration, tax-residency disputes, or unusual related-party transactions. Quantified risk of an unannounced physical inspection within the first 12 months is low, estimated at approximately 5 percent for a non-resident tax-exempt International Company, rising to about 15 percent if GST registration, high-risk PEP involvement, frequent related-party payments, or cross-border cash-equivalent transactions are present.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: The Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand), principally Sections 15–20 (incorporation and registration), Section 26 (constitution), Sections 128–130 (registered office and address for service), Sections 152–156 (director requirements and board proceedings), and Part VII (financial reporting); supplemented by the Companies (Registration) Regulations 1994 and the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) framework. The entity is constituted as a New Zealand-incorporated International Company (IC) with limited liability, designed for non-resident ownership and intended to qualify for Tax Exempt Zone treatment under the Income Tax Act 2007 with respect to foreign-sourced income of the company for non-resident shareholders.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Companies Register), a business unit of the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), operating the online register at https://www.companiesoffice.govt.nz and supporting the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) scheme.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of a Company (Form 2) submitted electronically on the NZ Companies Register portal, together with the Company Constitution (or the statutory default rules of Table 1 of the Companies Act 1993) and the Consents to Act as Director (Form 3) for each proposed director.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is prescribed by the Companies Act 1993. The company may be incorporated with one or more shares of any nominal value, commonly 1,000 ordinary shares at NZ$1.00 each fully paid-up. No escrow account, capital deposit, or paid-up capital verification is required by the Companies Office; share capital may be satisfied in cash or non-cash consideration upon allotment.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Company be and is hereby incorporated as a limited liability company under the Companies Act 1993, and that the Company Constitution presented to this meeting be adopted as the Company's Constitution, governing the internal management of the Company pursuant to Section 26 of the Act. RESOLVED FURTHER, that subscription for the initial issued capital of the Company be approved, such capital comprising 1,000 fully paid ordinary shares of NZ$1.00 each, subscribed for by the founding shareholders named in the Application for Registration, and that allotment of the said shares be recorded in the Company's Share Register upon issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office of the Company be, and the same is hereby, fixed at the address specified in the Application for Registration, and that the Registrar of Companies be notified thereof in accordance with Section 189 of the Companies Act 1993. RESOLVED FURTHER, that [INSERT FULL NAME] be and is hereby appointed sole Director, [INSERT FULL NAME] be appointed Chairperson, and [INSERT FULL NAME] be appointed Company Secretary of the Company, each to act until lawfully removed, and that such officers be authorized jointly and severally to open bank accounts, execute contracts, engage professional advisers, and take all such steps as may be necessary to complete incorporation and to commence lawful business.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-Incorporation Name Clearance and NZBN Pre-Assessment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office online portal and NZBN Register (https://www.companiesoffice.govt.nz)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a company name availability search on the Companies Register to confirm the proposed name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name and does not contain any restricted or prohibited expression under Sections 21–24 of the Companies Act 1993. Confirm that the name ends with 'Limited' or its approved abbreviation and that the nominated registered office address is a physical New Zealand address available for service of process. Name reservation is optional and can be executed as part of the incorporation application; if a premium name is required, file a name reservation request online before submitting Form 2.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name in order of preference
Registered office physical address and postal address for service in New Zealand
Details of founding shareholders (full legal name, date of birth, residential address, passport or national ID number for AML screening)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or reserved to another registrant, submit an alternative name online or file a written request for the Registrar to exercise discretion under Section 23 of the Companies Act 1993; a misleading name may also be made acceptable by adding a distinctive descriptor, corporate suffix, or NZBN number element.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting of Constitution, Officer Consents, and Corporate Governance Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Appointed New Zealand corporate law counsel or licensed incorporation service provider in coordination with the New Zealand Companies Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Company Constitution in accordance with Section 26 of the Companies Act 1993, covering share classes, director powers, board meeting procedures, indemnity and insurance, and dispute resolution, or adopt the default constitution in Table 1 of the Act. Prepare Form 3 Consents to Act as Director for each proposed director and ensure the statutory requirement that at least one director ordinarily resides in New Zealand (Section 152) is satisfied by appointing either a natural shareholder-director or a licensed nominee director resident in New Zealand. Confirm the registered office is a physical New Zealand address for service of process under Section 128 and record the same in the draft statutory registers.
required_dossiers: Company Constitution (or written election to adopt the Table 1 default rules)
Form 3 Consent to Act as Director for each proposed director
Share subscription letters and proposed share allotment schedule
AML/CFT verification pack for each director, shareholder, and beneficial owner (passport, proof of residential address, corporate ownership diagram)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar queries any constitutional provision or consent form, file an amended Constitution and re-executed consents electronically; a defective consent may be re-signed and resubmitted without restarting the entire incorporation, provided the statutory correction window remains available.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Submission of Application for Registration (Form 2)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office — Companies Register online filing system (Registrar of Companies)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the Application for Registration of a Company (Form 2) on the Companies Register portal, selecting the limited liability company type, entering the registered office, address for service, director and shareholder details, and the share structure. Attach or reference the Constitution and director consents, verify all data entries, and pay the statutory registration fee of NZ$71.43 (approximately USD 45) by electronic payment. Submit the application online; the Registrar processes approved applications and issues the Certificate of Incorporation with the company number, incorporation date, and the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN).
required_dossiers: Completed Form 2 application
Adopted Company Constitution in PDF (certified where requested)
Form 3 Consents to Act as Director
Identification certification or statutory declaration for each subscriber if prompted
Electronic payment confirmation of the registration fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried or rejected, the Companies Office will issue a deficiency notice; cure the deficiency by uploading corrected data or additional consents on the same portal, pay any resubmission fee if applicable, and re-file within the statutory correction window of 20 working days; alternatively file a fresh application with revised details.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation, NZBN Activation, and Establishment of Statutory Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office and NZBN Registrar
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon successful registration, the Companies Office issues the Certificate of Incorporation and activates the company's New Zealand Business Number (NZBN). The company must then establish the statutory share register, maintain minutes of board resolutions, record directors and the registered office in the public register, and preserve financial records as required under Sections 188–216 of the Companies Act 1993. Verify that the certificate name matches the reserved name and that all statutory notification timelines commence, including any requirement to notify Inland Revenue of tax registration.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation downloaded from the Companies Register
NZBN confirmation record
Statutory register templates (share register, director register, minutes book)
Initial board resolutions authorizing first business transactions and banking
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Certificate or register entry contains an error, apply to the Registrar for correction under Section 19 of the Companies Act 1993 by submitting certified corrected details and supporting evidence; a recalculation or reissuance of the NZBN can be requested through the NZBN service desk.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inland Revenue (IRD) and Tax Compliance Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue Department of New Zealand — online via myIR Business portal (https://www.ird.govt.nz)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company with Inland Revenue to obtain an IRD number, commence the provisional tax cycle, and register for GST if the company anticipates taxable supplies exceeding NZ$60,000 in a 12-month period or elects to register voluntarily. Register for employer obligations (PAYE, KiwiSaver, fringe benefit tax) if staff will be employed. For the International Company (IC) structure intended to operate under the Tax Exempt Zone classification, confirm with a tax advisor the eligibility requirements for foreign-sourced income exemption and file any required election, confirmation, or binding ruling application with Inland Revenue.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and NZBN
Director and shareholder tax residency declarations (IR742 and IR596 forms)
Business description referencing ISIC 4791 electronic catalogue retail of industrial MRO hardware and warehousing activity
Estimated turnover, GST election form, and bank account details for tax refunds
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the IRD registration is queried due to incomplete business address or unclear ownership information, correct the myIR business profile and resubmit; late registration penalties may be remitted upon voluntary disclosure under the Tax Administration Act 1994 where the omission arose from a genuine processing delay.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Physical Premises Licensing, Health and Safety Clearance, and Banking/AML Account Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Territorial Authority (e.g., Auckland Council), Fire and Emergency New Zealand (FENZ), WorkSafe New Zealand, and the Appointed Commercial Bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: For the B2B MRO distribution warehouse, coordinate with the local territorial authority to secure the required occupancy and building consent and a building Warrant of Fitness (WoF) verifying structural load and emergency egress under the Building Act 2004. Engage a Fire and Emergency New Zealand approved evacuation scheme auditor where the warehouse exceeds applicable occupancy thresholds. Implement a written Health and Safety at Work Act 2015 (HSWA) plan, hazard register, first aid kit, and worker induction records; where required, register the workplace with WorkSafe New Zealand. In order to open the company's trading account, present the Certificate of Incorporation, NZBN, constitutional documents, and an AML/CFT ownership declaration to the commercial bank; the bank will complete customer due diligence before activating the account.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and NZBN confirmation
Lease or premises title and building safety compliance documents
Building Warrant of Fitness and fire evacuation scheme approval where applicable
HSWA workplace plan and hazard register signed by the director
Banking due diligence pack (passport, proof of address, constitutional documents, beneficial ownership diagram, trading description)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If council, FENZ, or WorkSafe issues a compliance query, provide the structural engineer's report, fire safety consultant's certificate, or an abatement plan and apply for modification; WorkSafe improvement notices may be cured by filing a compliant corrective action plan within the notice period. A bank declining KYC clearance can be remedied by supplying refreshed beneficial-ownership charts, warehouse documentation, and transaction-flow descriptions to reduce the AML risk rating.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE) — Workforce and Business Systems directorate; WorkSafe New Zealand for workplace health and safety; the Local Territorial Authority (e.g., Auckland Council) for premises and warehousing consents; Fire and Emergency New Zealand (FENZ) for fire safety certification.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not separately licensed: the electronic catalogue retail operation of industrial MRO hardware (ISIC 4791) qualifies as a general unlicensed business activity. The operative authorizations are the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN), a building occupancy certificate and Warrant of Fitness under the Building Act 2004, a fire evacuation scheme where required, and a workplace safety system under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015. Storage of hazardous consumables above threshold quantities would additionally require an approval under the Hazardous Substances and New Organisms (HSNO) Act 1996.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) of New Zealand in coordination with the relevant Regional Council exercising consent authority under the Resource Management Act 1991
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration / permitted activity tier — no formal Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) report is mandated for a non-manufacturing wholesale e-commerce and warehousing facility. The operation is classified as a Permitted Activity under the National Environmental Standards (NES) for air quality and the regional air plan, requiring only premises registration with the Local Territorial Authority. A full Assessment of Environmental Effects (AEE) is triggered only if the facility expands into hazardous-substance storage above HSNO threshold quantities, installs heavy diesel back-up generation, or introduces industrial spray-painting or solvent-intensive operations.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: no industrial process discharge is generated by the warehouse; stormwater runoff must comply with the Regional Council discharge permit standards under the Resource Management Act 1991 and no MRO oil residues, lubricants, or chemical rinsates may enter council drains. Volatile Organic Compounds (VOCs): the facility is classified as a low-VOC emitter as it is distribution-only; storage of solvents and lubricants is capped at 5,000 litres or the relevant HSNO Class 3 threshold, and any storage above that requires an approved hazardous-substances location certificate. Solid waste: mandatory waste segregation, contracted disposal to a permitted landfill, and a waste-tracking manifest for oily rags, spent aerosols, and electronic components under the Waste Minimisation Act 2008 and the Hazardous Substances and New Organisms Regulations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certification under the Building Act 2004 and the Fire and Emergency New Zealand Act 2017: the warehouse must maintain a compliant fire egress system, extinguishing equipment, and, where the site stores combustible MRO goods or occupancy exceeds ten persons, an FENZ-approved evacuation scheme; evidence is the Building Warrant of Fitness (Form 12) audited annually by the Local Territorial Authority plus a fire safety verification statement. Structural Load Inspections: a registered structural engineer's certificate verifying racking and mezzanine floor load capacities, seismic compliance with the current New Zealand Building Code, and safe manual-handling zones. Workplace Clearance: WorkSafe New Zealand verification of the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015 system, comprising a hazard register, risk assessment for lifting equipment, first-aid certification, worker induction and training records, emergency spill-response kits, and a statement of fitness from the appointed occupational health advisor.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue (Te Tari Taake), New Zealand Government. Online portal: myIR (https://www.ird.govt.nz/myir/)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident or tax-exempt international company seeking to establish a tax presence in New Zealand must first obtain a New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) via the New Zealand Companies Office if it carries on business in New Zealand, and then apply to Inland Revenue for an IRD number. The standard application path for a foreign-incorporated or offshore-registered entity is Form IR742 (Registration for income tax and GST for non-resident companies) or the online non-resident company registration through myIR. The applicant must provide certified constitutional documents, board resolutions confirming the New Zealand agent or place of business, proof of registered office and director details, and a completed IRD number application. IRD numbers are generally issued within 5–10 working days. GST registration, if required or elected, is effected on the same IRD number through myIR or Form GST1A.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: New Zealand does not operate a check-the-box entity classification regime. The CK_IC, as an International Company under the applicable tax-exempt offshore regime, is automatically treated as a tax-exempt non-resident entity for New Zealand tax purposes: it is not subject to New Zealand income tax on foreign-source income and is not assessed on income derived outside New Zealand, provided it is not managed and controlled in New Zealand. The entity may voluntarily elect to register for New Zealand GST under section 51 of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985, and may elect to form part of a GST group under section 55 of that Act. No hybrid mismatch election is available; the BEPS hybrid mismatch rules operate to neutralise any tax benefit that would otherwise arise from differing entity characterisations.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST – Goods and Services Tax under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 of taxable supplies in any 12-month period; voluntary registration is available regardless of turnover
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: New Zealand has no mandatory real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping regime. GST returns and tax invoices are filed electronically through myIR or approved software. Use of the New Zealand Peppol e-Invoicing network is voluntary. Inland Revenue API services permit software providers to transmit GST returns and supporting data, but there is no government pre-clearance of invoices before issue.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating of exports applies to supplies of goods that are exported from New Zealand by the supplier, or supplied and delivered directly to a place outside New Zealand. For B2B electronic-catalog sales of industrial MRO hardware, the supply will be zero-rated if the supplier retains evidence that the goods left New Zealand within 12 months of the supply and that the customer is outside New Zealand. Services supplied to non-residents who are outside New Zealand at the time of supply and that are supplied in respect of goods situated outside New Zealand may also be zero-rated. The zero-rating is available only where the supplier has obtained the export documentation prescribed by Inland Revenue and the New Zealand Customs Service.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: New Zealand Customs Service Export Entry (Cargo Export Declaration)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill issued by the ocean or air carrier
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank statement evidencing receipt of funds in foreign currency from the overseas purchaser
Delivery confirmation or signed proof of arrival at the overseas destination
Copy of the customer's order and record of the offshore shipping terms
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Inland Revenue and the New Zealand Customs Service closely audit exported-supply claims. If the exporter cannot substantiate actual export or if goods are returned to New Zealand or diverted to domestic use, the zero-rating is retrospectively reversed and the supplier becomes liable for output GST at 15% on the original consideration, plus use-of-money interest. Shortfall penalties under the Tax Administration Act 1994 apply: 20% for failure to take reasonable care, 40% for gross carelessness, and 100% to 150% for evasion or fraudulent GST claims. Directors may be held personally liable for GST clawback and penalties in sham-export arrangements.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Te Pūtea Matua) — New Zealand's central bank and prudential regulator; the Financial Markets Authority (FMA) and the Department of Internal Affairs (DIA) jointly supervise AML/CFT obligations for banks, money remitters, and financial service providers.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand maintains a fully liberalised and freely convertible currency regime under the Currency Act 1983 and the Reserve Bank of New Zealand Act 2021, with no exchange-control legislation applicable to current-account or capital-account transactions. The New Zealand Dollar (NZD) is fully convertible on both the onshore and offshore markets, and there are no restrictions on the repatriation of dividends, branch profits, loan repayments, royalties, or invested capital. Non-resident foreign-currency accounts (USD, EUR, AUD, GBP, CNH, JPY) are routinely permitted without central-bank approval. Profit remittance from a New Zealand operational subsidiary or branch is subject only to Non-Resident Withholding Tax (NRWT) at treaty rates (typically 15% on dividends, 10% on interest, 5% on royalties under the NZ–Cook Islands double tax arrangements) and standard AML/CFT source-of-funds verification; no quantitative or temporal restrictions apply.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory requirement in New Zealand to surrender, deposit, or convert export proceeds into NZD. Exporters are free to retain foreign-currency receipts in any authorised foreign-currency account or to remit funds globally without central-bank conversion directives. The Reserve Bank of New Zealand and Stats NZ require only statistical reporting of cross-border merchandise trade (Overseas Merchandise Trade dataset) once cumulative values exceed the monthly reporting threshold, and all inward/outward international wire transfers are subject to the transaction-monitoring under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009. No mandatory conversion ratio, time limit, or exchange-rate obligation is imposed on the export sale of industrial MRO supplies.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: ANZ Business Multi-Currency Operating Account (NZD, USD, AUD, EUR) with segregated Capital Escrow Sub-Account for initial share-capital verification and merchant-acquiring settlement
BNZ Foreign Entity Business Transaction Account (NZD/USD) with BNZ Trade Finance Facility for Commercial LC issuance and FX forward line
Westpac Business Cash Management Account (NZD), Westpac Global Foreign Currency Account, and Merchant Services (card acquiring via Paymark)
ASB Business Transacting Account (NZD) with FastNet Classic internet banking and ASB Trade Solutions (import/export letters of credit)
Kiwibank Business Account (NZD only, no full multi-currency or LC capability)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: MEDIUM-HIGH for supplementary clearing rails, NOT a replacement for a Tier 1 transactional account. Off-shore digital financial institutions and EMIs — including Wise (originally NZ-founded), Airwallex, and Revolut Business — can provide efficient cross-border collection/payout channels for the B2B MRO e-commerce platform, including virtual USD/EUR receivables accounts and discounted supplier wire pricing. Legal constraints: (i) any EMI that performs money-remittance services in New Zealand must be registered on the Financial Service Providers Register (FSPR) and must appoint a NZ compliance officer under the AML/CFT Act 2009; (ii) an off-shore EMI without a NZ-licensed entity must rely on its home-country passporting or on a NZ money-changers licence, and settlement of merchant proceeds is normally restricted to a fully onboarded NZ bank account in the same legal name; (iii) the Cook Islands International Company (CK_IC) will be subject to full beneficial-ownership disclosure and source-of-funds verification by the EMI, and any threshold-based transaction limits may trigger enhanced due diligence, especially for high-velocity card-plus-wire flows.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: There is no statutory mandate requiring physical attendance, but Tier 1 bank policies impose quasi-mandatory in-person or video-verified identity procedures for a non-resident Cook Islands International Company. In practice: ANZ and BNZ permit fully remote onboarding, provided that the authorised director or beneficial owner completes a live video interview, submits a notarised passport copy plus a corporate-entity certificate and certificate of good standing from the Cook Islands Financial Supervisory Commission, and the corporate service provider (CSP) in Rarotonga confirms the company register. Westpac, ASB, and Kiwibank generally require a physical branch meeting, either with a director who is physically in New Zealand or with an approved NZ-based professional referee (lawyer, chartered accountant) who attests to the identity of the off-shore directors. The entire KYC/onboarding cycle typically takes 7–12 business days; if a local NZ-resident director is resident, the timeline may compress to 4–7 business days. Non-face-to-face onboarding will automatically trigger enhanced due diligence under section 22 of the AML/CFT Act.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Shell-company red flag: zero physical premises in New Zealand, no local employees, all directors resident in Rarotonga, and no verifiable source of commercial turnover.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide: (i) registered-office certificate and current CSP services agreement from a licensed Cook Islands trustee; (ii) a third-party logistics agreement or short-term sub-lease in Auckland proving operational substance for warehousing and fulfilment; (iii) an executed supplier distribution agreement with an MRO wholesale principal demonstrating genuine trade flow; (iv) two years of management accounts or audited financial statements showing real e-commerce transactions; (v) director CVs, proof of address, and professional references; (vi) a flow-of-funds model distinguishing merchant card collections from supplier wire outflows.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore tax-haven jurisdiction perception: Cook Islands appears on the EU's list of non-cooperative jurisdictions and may be tagged by internal bank watchlists, triggering enhanced sanctions and tax-evasion screening.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit: (i) a confirmatory letter from the Cook Islands Registrar of International Companies attesting good standing and that the entity is a tax-exempt International Company with no active tax liabilities; (ii) evidence of Cook Islands' full participation in CRS/AEOI and its TIEA with New Zealand; (iii) an independent tax opinion confirming the structure is not used to evade NZ income tax and that the CK_IC is not managed-and-controlled from NZ; (iv) the ECB/EU Council delisting status if the Cook Islands is removed from Annex II; (v) a written commercial justification for the use of a Cook Islands IC (asset protection, succession planning, and trade contract neutrality).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO is a New Zealand tax resident or holds New Zealand residency status, creating a severe risk that the bank will deem the company resident in NZ and demand full NZ tax reporting, VAT/GST registration, and local payroll compliance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide: (i) board resolutions showing executive meetings physically held in Rarotonga (or by teleconference with a quorum physically present there); (ii) a directors' residence register demonstrating at least two directors are Cook Islands tax residents; (iii) a sworn certificate of central management and control from the local CSP; (iv) a New Zealand specialist tax opinion confirming that the IC is a foreign company for NZ tax purposes and not subject to income tax on foreign-sourced income; (v) if applicable, an NZ GST registration certificate (only if local supplies exceed NZD 60,000) and evidence of a tax agent appointment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume, low-value card + wire transaction pattern typical of wholesale distribution and e-commerce (ISIC 4791 / NAICS 423840), which raises potential money-laundering typology of 'trade-based money laundering' or invoice manipulation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver: (i) a complete list of the top 20 suppliers and 20 customers with legal names, countries, and contract reference numbers; (ii) sample invoices, packing lists, and shipping documentation (bill of lading/airway bill) for the last 12 months of trade; (iii) an independent compliance program, including a sanctions/PE/PEP screening manual; (iv) a signed auditor's report confirming that 100% of outbound wires correspond to a verified commercial invoice; (v) a reasonable-pricing benchmark (e.g., market index for MRO consumables) to demonstrate arm's-length invoicing.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound capital injection for the CK_IC is routed exclusively via SWIFT MT103 from the existing beneficial owner's account (or the Cook Islands trust's trustee account) directly into the ANZ or BNZ operational account under the exact remittance reference: 'SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION — [ENTITY NAME] — UBO NAME'. The bank will approve the credit only after verification of: (i) a board resolution authorising the issue of shares and designating the proposed capital amount; (ii) a signed share subscription agreement and share register extract; (iii) a source-of-wealth questionnaire confirming the funds originate from legitimate profits or savings; (iv) a trust deed extract (if a trust is the immediate shareholder) showing the trustee's power to capitalise the company; (v) a completed NZ CRS self-certification (identical to a W-8BEN-E). New Zealand imposes no exchange-control approval on inward capital; the receiving bank will apply the daily interbank FX rate if conversion into NZD is required. A minimum initial capital of NZD 100,000 is recommended to support the MRO inventory cycle and to satisfy the bank's economic-substance review. The capital must be held for a minimum of 90 days before any outbound distribution, and the bank will not permit early repayment to the shareholder without a formal resolution and tax clearance.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rails for outbound trade settlements: (a) SWIFT MT103 — used for 75% of supplier payments up to USD 250,000, with full OFAC/sanctions screening and the corresponding 'PURPOSE OF PAYMENT' field referencing the commercial invoice and purchase order; (b) Commercial Letters of Credit (MT700) — utilised for large-bulk purchases above USD 100,000 from overseas MRO manufacturers, issued via BNZ or ASB trade desks, with sight drafts and required documents (packing list, SGS inspection certificate, bill of lading) and a standard discrepancy tolerance of 10%; (c) MT202/MT2xx interbank transfers — applicable only where the supplier requests payment to a third-party nostro account, subject to an additional declaration of the underlying trade; (d) Merchant card settlement — the e-commerce platform's card receivables (Visa/Mastercard/Amex) settle via Windcave or bank acquiring services directly into the ANZ/BNZ operational account within T+2 for domestic cards and T+3 for international cards, followed by a manual supplier wire release. Currency netting is performed weekly: all USD supplier invoices are offset against USD card receivables before conversion into NZD, reducing FX frictions and capture spread. All disbursements are recorded in a single treasury workstation with automated audit trails for exemption from UBO transaction scrutiny.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable FX forwards (NZD/USD, NZD/AUD, NZD/EUR, NZD/GBP, NZD/JPY) executed under an ISDA 2002 New Zealand Master Agreement with a credit support annex (cash collateral of 5–10% of notional) and a tenor of up to 12 months.

FX swaps (same-day, tom/next, and spot/forward) authorised for balance-sheet liquidity equalisation on both the NZD operating account and the USD multi-currency sub-account, with no hedging ratio cap by the RBNZ.

Cross-currency basis swaps converting USD-denominated supplier payables into NZD fixed/floating interest obligations, permissible for non-residents without any regulatory restrictions, provided the bank holds sufficient NZD funding lines.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for illiquid emerging-market currencies (e.g., Chinese Yuan (CNH), Indonesian Rupiah, Thai Baht) utilised exclusively for hedging supplier invoices in non-convertible currencies; note that NZD is fully deliverable and NZD/NDFs are not offered by NZ banks.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due annually on the anniversary of incorporation; the Companies Office issues a reminder 10 weeks before the due date and accepts filings from that date until the anniversary date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fee of NZD 149.30 (approximately USD 94) applies after the due date; continued default after a Registrar's notice under section 209 of the Companies Act 1993 exposes the company to administrative strike-off under section 214, typically effectuated 20 working days after the final notice.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Form IR4) and Provisional Tax Reconciliation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 7 July following the standard 31 March balance date; extended to 31 March of the following year where a tax agent holds an extension of time arrangement.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of NZD 250 (approximately USD 158); late payment penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus incremental 1% per month; use-of-money interest accrues daily on underpayments until resolution.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory independent audit is mandatory for Financial Market Conduct (FMC) reporting entities and for 'large' companies defined under the Financial Reporting Act 2013, i.e., entities exceeding total assets of NZD 60 million or total revenue of NZD 30 million in each of the two preceding accounting periods; smaller non-reporting companies are exempt unless shareholders resolve to appoint an auditor or an external party contractually requires an audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Financial statements must comply with the New Zealand Accounting Standards Framework issued by the External Reporting Board (XRB): NZ IFRS (Tier 1), NZ IFRS Reduced Disclosure Regime (Tier 2), or the simplified NZ GAAP framework for Tier 3/Tier 4 entities; non-reporting small companies may prepare special-purpose financial statements for tax compliance purposes.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: New Zealand does not currently maintain a standalone annual UBO filing for ordinary private companies; beneficial ownership is instead confirmed through the Companies Office annual return, which requires updated director and shareholder details. Every share transfer must be recorded in the Register of Members without unreasonable delay, and the register must remain available for inspection at the registered office. Entities subject to the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 must conduct ongoing customer due diligence, including refreshing beneficial ownership information on a risk-sensitive basis and upon any change in shareholding control.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book (Board and Shareholder Meeting Minutes)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 250–750 per annum for registered office and company secretarial service
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,000–20,000 per annum for a small-to-mid-market trading entity subject to a full audit; reduced for specific engagement agreed upon by shareholders

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays are available under New Zealand domestic law. The Cook Islands International Company (IC) component enjoys a statutory zero-rate in the Cook Islands under the International Companies Act, but this exemption does not shield New Zealand-source income. Where the IC is managed and controlled from New Zealand, the full worldwide income becomes assessable at 28%. Available incentives include: the Research and Development Tax Incentive (a 15% refundable credit on eligible R&D expenditure), immediate expensing of qualifying low-value plant and equipment, and full deductibility of ordinary business expenses (COGS, payment-processing fees, freight, wages, depreciation and amortisation of e-commerce catalogue software). Effective tax rates in a B2B MRO e-commerce model are typically reduced below 28% by these deductions.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited – New Zealand permits indefinite carry-forward of tax losses under ITA 2007 s IA 5, subject to shareholder continuity of at least 49% or the business continuity (same-or-similar business) test. There is no 5-year expiry in New Zealand.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IR4 – Company Income Tax Return; filed electronically via Inland Revenue's myIR portal (mandatory for registered tax agents; paper IR4 restricted to limited cases).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (income year matching the balance date). Companies carrying on business in New Zealand also pay provisional tax in three instalments during the year (for a 31 March balance date: 28 August, 15 January and 7 May) using either the standard uplift method, the estimation method, or the GST-ratio method.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For the standard 31 March balance date, the IR4 return must be furnished by 7 July of the same income year. Where a registered tax agent represents the company, the filing deadline is extended to 31 March of the following year. Any terminal tax balance is due on 7 April following the balance date (extended proportionally when a tax agent holds an extension of time).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, NZBN, registered office (physical address), postal address, phone numbers and New Zealand IRD number.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Cook Islands IC's exact registered name as recorded with the Cook Islands Financial Supervisory Commission. The New Zealand registered office must be a physical address, not a PO Box. If the IC operates a branch or agency in New Zealand, state the branch's street address here.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Country in which the company is resident for tax purposes, determined by incorporation and by central management and control.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Cook Islands IC whose directors' meetings, strategic decisions and day-to-day control are exercised from New Zealand must declare New Zealand as its country of residence. A non-resident declaration (Cook Islands) is sustainable only where central management and control is genuinely exercised in the Cook Islands; maintain minutes, travel records and decision logs to support this.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: ANZSIC 4-digit industry code corresponding to the principal business activity.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use ANZSIC code 4520 (Electronic Shopping) for the B2B MRO catalogue e-commerce activity. Ensure the ANZSIC code is internally consistent with the ISIC 4791 classification used in corporate records and with the company's licence exemptions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross income derived from business during the income year, including online B2B sales of industrial maintenance hardware, freight surcharges and any related services.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident IC must include only income sourced in New Zealand: sales where the contracts are concluded in New Zealand, inventory held in New Zealand, or orders fulfilled through a New Zealand dependent agent. Foreign orders routed through the IC's offshore principal are excluded only if the New Zealand operation does not perform the core income-earning activities.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible expenditure classified by category: advertising, bad debts, contractors, depreciation, insurance, interest, legal fees, motor vehicles, office administration, other, rent/lease, repairs/maintenance, salaries/wages, travel and staff-related costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduct only expenses incurred in deriving assessable New Zealand-source income. Head-office allocations from the Cook Islands entity must be at arm's length and supported by a functional analysis and transfer pricing documentation. Credit-card and SWIFT payment-processing fees are deductible, as is MRO warehouse rent and freight.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net assessable profit or loss, being Box 12 less Box 13, before any tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the New Zealand branch records a loss, attach a breakdown of intercompany charges. A persistent-loss position inconsistent with the global MRO profit of the group attracts transfer pricing scrutiny.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-deductible items added back to net profit: fines, non-commercial expenditure, non-deductible royalties, imputation debits and expenditure not in connection with producing assessable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back any management fees, IP royalties or service charges paid to the Cook Islands IC that are not economically incurred or that exceed the arm's length amount. Unsubstantiated payments risk being treated as dividends.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Subsequent-year deductions and previous-year tax losses applied against the current year's assessable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident IC may claim New Zealand losses only from a New Zealand-source business, and only if the same business is carried on with the required ownership continuity. Losses incurred offshore by the IC cannot be offset against New Zealand branch income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net result after addbacks and deductions, representing the amount subject to income tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This is the figure on which tax at 28% is computed. A nil or negative figure must be supported by full accounting records to avoid recharacterization by Inland Revenue.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax on taxable income at the 28% corporate rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident ICs are taxed at the same 28% rate on New Zealand-source taxable income; no reduced branch-profit remittance tax exists in New Zealand.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credits to offset against the tax calculation: resident withholding tax (RWT) on interest/dividends received, PAYE deductions, imputation credits attached to dividends, foreign tax credits and provisional tax paid.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident IC may claim foreign tax credits for any income tax paid in the Cook Islands, limited to the New Zealand tax payable on the same income. Attach the relevant foreign tax credit calculation and supporting certificates.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Remaining tax payable or the excess of credits over tax payable, being the terminal tax balance or refund.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Where provisional tax instalments exceed the final liability, a refund will be issued. Where a non-resident IC has no New Zealand business presence, file a nil IR4 or a formal cessation notice to preclude a continuing New Zealand tax residency claim.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late Filing Penalty: NZD 150 immediately, plus NZD 50 per month for each month the return remains outstanding (maximum NZD 500) for standard taxpayers; large taxpayers face an initial NZD 500 penalty plus NZD 100 per month (maximum NZD 2,500). Late Payment Penalty: 1% of the unpaid tax imposed on the due date, an additional 4% if tax remains unpaid after 7 days, and further 4% increments every 6 months. Use of Money Interest (UOMI) under the Tax Administration Act 1994 s 120 accrues daily on all overdue amounts at the current underpayment rate.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: The statutory New Zealand Non-Resident Withholding Tax (NRWT) on dividends is 30%, reduced to 15% where the dividend is fully imputed (with imputation credits attached at the 28% company rate). Under most New Zealand double tax agreements, the rate is 15% for portfolio shareholdings and 5% for corporate shareholders owning at least 10% of the voting power (e.g., the New Zealand-Cook Islands arrangement and OECD-pattern treaties).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply a DTA-reduced dividend rate, the New Zealand payer must obtain and retain a Certificate of Residence (CoR) issued by the tax authority of the recipient's country of residence before payment is made. No advance approval from Inland Revenue is required, but the CoR must be genuine, cover the dividend payment date, and be kept in the payer's tax records. If the CoR is not obtained, the payer must withhold the statutory NRWT (15% for fully imputed dividends) and the recipient may file a refund claim with Inland Revenue on Form IR3/foreign withholding tax refund schedule. For interest and royalties, the payer must also document the beneficial ownership of the recipient; an Approved Issuer Levy (AIL) election at 2% may be filed with Inland Revenue in lieu of NRWT on qualifying interest paid to unrelated or related non-resident lenders under registered securities.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory NRWT of 15% applies to New Zealand-source royalties (including payments for the use of trademarks, software licences and technical know-how). Most New Zealand DTAs reduce the rate to 10%, with certain treaties providing 5% for copyright royalties for cultural purposes. Interest: statutory NRWT on interest paid to a non-resident lender is 15%; an Approved Issuer Levy (AIL) of 2% may be elected instead of NRWT for interest on registered securities, which is typical for intercompany SWIFT-funded loans where the lender is a non-resident and the borrower is an approved issuer. No NRWT applies to interest on securities quoted on the official list of a recognised exchange.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: New Zealand Inland Revenue's administrative transfer pricing documentation threshold: an aggregate value of cross-border related-party transactions exceeding NZD 10 million per income year triggers the expectation that a Local File be prepared and retained. A Master File is expected where the multinational group's total consolidated revenue exceeds NZD 100 million, and Country-by-Country Reporting applies to groups with consolidated revenue exceeding approximately NZD 1.13 billion. Despite these administrative thresholds, the Tax Administration Act 1994 s 51(4)(c) requires every taxpayer to retain sufficient transfer pricing records to enable the Commissioner to verify that related-party dealings are on an arm's length basis, even where no contemporaneous Local File is prepared.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: New Zealand has no standalone Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) analogous to those of offshore financial centres; however, the general anti-avoidance rule in ITA 2007 s BG 1, the purpose test in s GA 1, the sham doctrine and the central management and control test operate to deny tax advantages where an entity lacks commercial substance. A Cook Islands IC holding MRO e-commerce income without a real office, employees, decision-making autonomy or direct operational function will be challenged. The explicit tax-exempt classification of the Cook Islands IC does not extend to New Zealand-source income, and if the IC is managed and controlled from New Zealand it will be treated as a New Zealand-resident company taxable on its worldwide income at 28%.
